items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: my brother turned into be Cornelius Wooding he turned into be one of the finest doctors in Philadelphia.

ctx.x: No, I'll tell you. If he was in music, he kept it quiet. I never knew that. And I'll tell you why. How he -- he was a lover of his own people. So, when we heard- I must have been about six or seven years old, when he heard there was a colored show coming to town, he immediately got his wife, my mother, and the four children together and took us to the theater. But, at that time, we were not in Philadelphia, because every summer he worked in Atlantic City at the Brighton Hotel. And by working at the Brighton…

Before that, I was supposed to be a dentist, in their mind. My one brother was supposed to be a doctor. My older brother was supposed to be a preacher, and my sister was supposed to be a nurse. But, only two of these things happened. That is, my brother turned into be Cornelius Wooding he turned into be one of the finest doctors in Philadelphia. And I turned out to be a hambone musician in Atlantic City.
